data.title: Here's what India's mutual funds bought and sold in October
data.description:
India's Mutual Funds remained net buyers in October, buying equities worth ₹42,500 crore, in a month before the turnaround began for the markets, pushing the banking index to a record high. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold ₹34,200 crore, as per Nuvama Alternative and Quantitative Research. Following are all the major additions, reductions, new purchases and exits by some of the mutual funds in October, as per Nuvama Alternative:

SBI MF | India's largest fund house bought shares of ITC (₹1,380 crore), Jio Platforms (₹803 crore), and Hindustan Aeronautics (₹793 crore). It trimmed its stake in financials and auto companies like Bajaj Finance (₹718 crore), Kotak Mahindra Bank (₹716 crore), and Bajaj Auto (₹700 crore). Fresh purchases were made in new listings like Paras Healthcare, while the fund made a complete exit from Rainbow Children, Lodha and L&T Finance.

Aditya Birla Sun Life MF | The fund house bought shares worth ₹583 crore in Jio Platforms during the month of October. Persistent Systems was also a big buy for the fund with a purchase of ₹330 crore. Tata Group's Trent was also on the buy list of the fund this month (₹247 crore). It reduced stake in Bharti Airtel (₹753 crore), Reliance Industries (₹453 crore), and Infosys (₹390 crore) during the month. Bonfiglioli Transmissions was another fresh purchase during the month by the fund during October.

HDFC MF | Max Healthcare was a major purchase for the fund house in October, as it bought shares worth ₹583 crore, according to Nuvama Alternative. The other major purchases included Jio Platforms (₹523 crore), and HDFC Bank (₹442 crore). Major reductions last month included HCLTech (₹886 crore), Axis Bank (₹804 crore), and Life Insurance Corporation of India (₹434 crore). Fresh purchases were made by the fund in Triveni Turbine, PTC Industries and Shree Cement, while Gulf Oil, Laser Power, and Uniparts India were complete exits.

ICICI Prudential MF | ITC continued to be favoured by fund houses in October, with ICICI Prudential MF also making a ₹2,574 crore purchase in the stock last month. Its other major purchases included M&M (₹1,117 crore), and Bajaj Finserv (₹963 crore). It reduced its stake in Infosys (₹2,271 crore), Kotak Mahindra Bank (₹1,722 crore), and Bharti Airtel (₹1,462 crore). Fresh purchases were made in Jio Platforms, M&M Financial, Fusion Finance and Ather Energy, while GNA Axles, Atlanta Electricals, and Alivus Life Sciences were complete exits.

Kotak MF | Jio Platforms shares worth ₹690 crore were purchased by the fund house, who also increased its stake in Infosys (₹459 crore) and Adani Enterprises (₹442 crore). Major reductions were made in Bharti Airtel (₹657 crore), Coforge (₹657 crore) and Cholamandalam Investment (₹636 crore). Its fresh purchases were in Colgate-Palmolive, Fusion Finance and Wipro. It completely exited from CMR Green, Prestige Estats and Pfizer.

Axis MF | Its major additions included a purchase of shares worth ₹388 crore of Tech Mahindra, worth ₹381 crore of Ather Energy and ₹362 crore of BSE. Its major reductions comprised of a ₹194 crore sale of Torrent Power's shares, ₹171 crore worth of Pidilite's shares, and ₹156 crore worth Mankind Pharma's shares. It freshly purchased stakes in Jio Platforms and Bonfiglioli Transmission, while it completely exited from Triveni Turbine, Bharat Dynamics and SBI Funds.

data.title: Anthropic's Mega IPO Lives Up to Wall Street Hype but Fails to Revive AI Trade — WSJ
data.description:
By Corrie Driebusch, Kate Clark and Hannah Erin Lang

From Wall Street's perspective, Anthropic's long-awaited stock-market debut did everything it had to: The largest initial public offering ever raised tens of billions to fund the artificial-intelligence giant's audacious plans and bestowed its early backers with eye-popping profits.

The company and its advisers pulled it off just as investors were beginning to sour on AI-related stocks, questioning whether massive, economy-shaping investments in the industry would pay off soon — and as public backlash to the sector grew. The shock resignation of Nvidia's Jensen Huang after a sex-and-spy scandal added to the market unease.

But investors big and small plowed into Anthropic's shares anyway, viewing it as a company too central to the AI universe to ignore. The shares began trading a little before noon Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and closed up 17%, giving the company a market value of around $1.3 trillion, or around $1.8 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

The stock had opened more than 30% above the IPO price of $83, but the gains fizzled throughout the day. Some investors are already questioning if the unprofitable company can sustain its extraordinary pace of revenue growth and weather the growing threat of open-source software companies, which offer cheaper AI tools.

In another sign investors remain wary of tech and AI stocks, major indexes declined Thursday, led by the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite, which dropped 2.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average logged its fourth straight day of declines, losing 2.2%, or 1,101 points. The S&P 500 dropped 2% to extend its losing streak to six sessions, with all 11 sectors of the index finishing in the red.

"By any means, Anthropic's IPO was a success," said Renos Savvides, head of equity capital markets at investment-management firm Neuberger. "But this was looked at as a barometer for the AI trade, for the IPO market and for the broader market itself. By that measure, the jury is still out."

Anthropic's market debut at the Nasdaq, complete with a billboard takeover of Times Square, caps a rapid rise for a company founded in 2021 that was worth around $20 billion as recently as 2024. Its Claude chatbot and the virality of its Claude Code coding tools have propelled it to new heights, and along the way helped reshape how people work, hunt for information and learn.

Each of Anthropic's seven co-founders, a group of former OpenAI employees that includes siblings Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, are now worth over $20 billion apiece. The Amodeis and the other co-founders have pledged to donate 80% of their personal equity in the company to charity, in keeping with the company's avowed focus on AI safety and public benefit.

The IPO provoked a backlash from some AI safety advocates who argue Anthropic has turned its back on its safety commitments. An open letter this week called for rejection of Anthropic's "reckless attempt to amass power in the name of greater good."

Jacob Coxon, an Anthropic researcher who sparked global anxiety about AI risks when he quit Anthropic in September, appeared Thursday at a protest in front of Anthropic's headquarters to call for a ban on self-improving AI systems.

"We're here because this technology is threatening our lives," Coxon told the crowd. A protest also took place near the Nasdaq in New York.

The offering, which raised $81 billion and topped the previous IPO record set by SpaceX's June listing, will add to the massive war chest Anthropic is building to fund some $900 billion of commitments to secure computing power and data center capacity. Anthropic raised an additional $26 billion from big companies including Nvidia, Google and Advanced Micro Devices in a private placement alongside the offering.

Nearly two dozen banks worked on the IPO, with the top two, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, each earning fees of over $110 million.

The relatively smooth IPO — and fervent investor appetite — increases pressure on rival OpenAI, which once held the advantage, to move quickly on its own plans to go public as soon as next year.

Many on Wall Street and in Silicon Valley jockeyed for pieces of the IPO. Big institutions ranging from asset managers and hedge funds to venture-capital firms put in large orders and some were turned away.

Investing giant BlackRock received about half of the roughly $10 billion allocation it requested, according to people familiar with the matter.

Investors who bought at the IPO price were sitting on modest gains Thursday, while many early venture-capital investors in Anthropic including Lightspeed Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures reaped billions. Some individuals who bought shares at the open or shortly after the stock began trading might not be so lucky.

Ben Pfeiffer, a 45-year old entrepreneur, was sitting in his home office in New Braunfels, Texas, his eyes glued to his screen to catch the first few seconds of Anthropic trading. He had received only four of the 200 shares he requested via Robinhood, and was hoping to snap up some more. But as he watched the stock's early gains reverse soon after its debut, he decided against it.

Pfeiffer said he's still bullish on Anthropic long term — he has used Claude to build and run his business — but he's waiting for shares to drop further before buying more.

He had already thought Anthropic was "brave" for going through with its offering in this market.

"People are just really cautious right now," he said, citing recent stock declines and a string of prominent tech outages. "They're thinking 'Why would I want to invest in this technology that's making my life worse?'"

Write to Corrie Driebusch at corrie.driebusch@wsj.com, Kate Clark at kate.clark@wsj.com and Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com

data.title: UK GfK consumer sentiment edges up after October slump
data.description:
British consumer sentiment edged up in November as shoppers prepared to make big purchases during Black Friday promotions, after recording its sharpest fall since the COVID-19 pandemic in October.

The GfK consumer confidence index, Britain's longest-running monthly sentiment gauge, rose 2 points to -22 in November, in line with economists' median expectation in a Reuters poll, after falling 11 points in October to a six-month low of -24 .

"Following last month's dramatic fall in confidence, there is some welcome relief," said GfK consumer insights director Neil Bellamy. "That should reassure manufacturers and retailers ahead of the crucial Black Friday and Christmas trading period that there are still people out there willing to spend."

  • The biggest improvement in the index was in the major purchases component, which rose by 5 points to -17 in November after falling to a two-year low in October

  • Households' assessment of the general economic situation and its outlook improved, while their assessment of their personal financial situation worsened slightly

  • GfK said households were under pressure from inflation and rising interest rates

  • Earlier this month, the Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in over three years and forecast inflation would rise to nearly 5% in mid 2027

  • GfK's data was based on a survey of 2,009 people aged 16 and over between October 29 and November 13

data.title: U.K. Consumer Confidence Picks Up Despite Rising Headwinds
data.description:
By Don Nico Forbes

U.K. consumer sentiment recovered slightly in November, though inflation concerns and higher interest rates are set to continue weighing on household budgets in the coming months.

Research group GfK said its consumer-confidence barometer, published Friday with the Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions, rose 2 points to minus 22 in the month. The data follows a steep fall in confidence last month amid rising cost-of-living pressures.

The pickup in sentiment for November was driven largely by consumers' willingness to make major purchases, said Neil Bellamy, consumer insights director at GfK.

"That should reassure manufacturers and retailers ahead of the crucial Black Friday and Christmas trading period that there are still people out there willing to spend," he said.

Perceptions of the economy also improved, though confidence for both the year ahead and the past 12 months remained firmly in negative territory. Meanwhile, sentiment surrounding personal finances continued to soften, pointing to vulnerability to economic uncertainty in the coming months, Bellamy said.

"Consumers were already grappling with persistent inflationary pressures, and higher interest rates are likely to have placed additional strain on household budgets," he said.

The Bank of England raised its key interest rate to 4.00% from 3.75% earlier this month, and left the door open for further hikes in the months ahead as higher energy prices driven by the war between the U.S. and Iran continue to push inflation far above the central bank's 2% target.

Consumer price growth rose to 3.6% in October. The BOE expects inflation to rise to 5% next year, with an anticipated jump in household energy bills in January likely to stretch consumer budgets further. Still, the central bank has said it hasn't yet seen evidence of higher energy prices feeding through to other areas of the economy. Core inflation remained unchanged in October, while food and nonalcoholic beverage inflation fell to its lowest level since 2021.

Resilient consumer spending has supported economic growth this year, but economists say consistently depressed household confidence could dampen hopes of a strong and sustainable recovery.

data.title: California Attorney General Issues Investigative Subpoena to Nvidia — WSJ
data.description:
By Jennifer Calfas

California's attorney general issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia on Thursday, opening a probe into the conduct of the embattled chip maker following the exposure of former chief executive Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta said his office is asking the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company whether its powerful chips, or any confidential information, were shared with China. The California Department of Justice is also seeking to determine whether Nvidia misled investors and the public.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags," Bonta said in a statement. The information, his office said, would be used to determine whether the company violated state law.

"Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta said.

A spokesperson for Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Nvidia, a stock-market juggernaut at the center of the booming artificial-intelligence industry, has been under scrutiny since a fast-moving scandal involving the company's star chief executive prompted his ouster. Huang resigned from Nvidia last week after extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who U.S. authorities suspect of working for Chinese state intelligence.

The Securities and Exchange Commission is also investigating Nvidia, The Wall Street Journal has reported. Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress in December, according to lawmakers.

Write to Jennifer Calfas at jennifer.calfas@wsj.com

data.title: Japan Consumer Prices Jump 0.8% In October
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - Overall consumer prices in Japan spiked 0.8 percent on month in October, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications said on Friday.

That was well above forecasts for an increase of 0.3 percent following the flat reading in September.

On a yearly basis, inflation was up 2.3 percent, above forecasts for 2.2 percent and up from 2.1 percent in the previous month.

Core CPI, which strips out the volatile costs of fresh food, was up 2.2 percent on year. That was shy of expectations for an increase of 2.3 percent and was up from 2.1 percent a month earlier.

data.title: Mesoblast Wins Deloitte Tech Fast 50 Leadership & Enterprise Growth Award
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mesoblast Limited (Nasdaq:MESO; ASX:MSB), global leader in allogeneic cellular medicines for inflammatory diseases, today announced it has received the Leadership & Enterprise Growth Award at the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 Australia Awards which recognizes Australia’s fastest-growing technology companies and the founders, innovators and leaders shaping the future of the sector.

The award recognizes Mesoblast’s successful evolution to a commercial-stage biotechnology company following its U.S. launch of Ryoncil® (remestemcel-L-rknd), the first mesenchymal stromal cell therapy approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).1

“We are pleased to receive this award from Deloitte which recognizes Mesoblast's leadership excellence across innovation and scalability in the healthcare industry,” said Mesoblast Chief Executive Dr. Silviu Itescu. “The successful launch of RYONCIL has established a strong commercial foundation for Mesoblast and has enabled patients to access a life changing product. We are focused on building on that foundation, progressing our broader portfolio and delivering sustainable growth and long-term value for our shareholders.”

About Mesoblast

Mesoblast (the Company) is a world leader in developing allogeneic (off-the-shelf) cellular medicines for the treatment of severe and life-threatening inflammatory conditions. The therapies from the Company’s proprietary mesenchymal lineage cell therapy technology platform respond to severe inflammation by releasing anti-inflammatory factors that counter and modulate multiple effector arms of the immune system, resulting in significant reduction of the damaging inflammatory process.

Mesoblast’s Ryoncil® (remestemcel-L-rknd) for the treatment of steroid-refractory acute graft versus host disease (SR-aGvHD) in pediatric patients 2 months and older is the first FDA-approved mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy. Please see the full Prescribing Information at www.ryoncil.com.

Mesoblast is committed to developing additional cell therapies for distinct indications based on its remestemcel-L and rexlemestrocel-L allogeneic stromal cell technology platforms. Ryoncil® is being developed for additional inflammatory diseases including SR-aGvHD in adults and biologic-resistant inflammatory bowel disease. Rexlemestrocel-L is being developed for heart failure and chronic low back pain. The Company has established commercial partnerships in Japan, Europe and China.

About Mesoblast intellectual property: Mesoblast has a strong and extensive global intellectual property portfolio, with over 1,000 granted patents or patent applications covering mesenchymal stromal cell compositions of matter, methods of manufacturing and indications. These granted patents and patent applications provide commercial protection extending through to at least 2044 in all major markets.

About Mesoblast manufacturing: The Company’s proprietary manufacturing processes yield industrial-scale, cryopreserved, off-the-shelf, cellular medicines. These cell therapies, with defined pharmaceutical release criteria, are planned to be readily available to patients worldwide.

Mesoblast has locations in Australia, the United States and Singapore and is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (MSB) and on the Nasdaq (MESO). For more information, please see www.mesoblast.com, LinkedIn: Mesoblast Limited and X: @Mesoblast

data.title: After Anthropic's 'bittersweet' IPO, here's what lies ahead
data.description:
By William Gavin

Retail investors showed up, but Anthropic has so far failed to provide a broad lift to the technology sector

Anthropic just debuted on the Nasdaq.

The true test of Anthropic's initial public offering lies in the weeks and months ahead - when more investors will have the ability to both buy and sell shares in a referendum on the state of artificial intelligence.

Anthropic ended up selling more shares than expected in its IPO - and at a higher price - as its stock debuted Thursday on the Nasdaq. In terms of proceeds, Anthropic (ANT) had the biggest IPO to date, breaking SpaceX's (SPCX) record and leaving the company with ample coffers to help fund the AI boom.

However, the stock's early momentum faded on Thursday, ending the day up just 17% from its IPO price. Shares had opened 34% higher before giving back some gains.

Anthropic had a non-diluted market capitalization of $1.28 trillion at the close.

Some people may "call it lackluster next to other tech IPOs, but it's debatable whether a bigger pop is desirable, since that could suggest Anthropic left more money on the table," said James Kisner, an analyst at Water Tower Research, via email.

Kisner added that the IPO's execution was "bittersweet," since it poured cold water on the idea that Anthropic could lift the broader market.

Anthropic went public in less-than-ideal conditions, with fear over everything from high inflation to Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO succession struggles and concerns over export policies weighing down on stocks. Kieran Osborne, chief investment officer at Mission Wealth, noted some investors may have trimmed their other tech stakes to buy Anthropic shares.

According to Dow Jones Market Data, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, S&P 500 SPX, Nasdaq Composite COMP and Russell 2000 RUT are each on pace for their worst week since April 4, 2025.

While Anthropic may not be the tide that raises all boats, the IPO still represents an "important milestone" for the AI sector, said Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson. After all is said and done, Anthropic will also have more than $230 billion in cash, based on the details of its IPO and its latest financial statements.

"Anthropic now has an enormous war chest it can use to buy more compute from its providers, primarily Amazon, Google and SpaceX. Those companies in turn now have visibility to buy more chips from Broadcom, Nvidia and Micron," Luria told MarketWatch over email. Compute refers to chips and other hardware.

Nick Smith, an analyst at Renaissance Capital, said Anthropic's "pretty strong debut" also is a good signal for future IPOs. He noted that several companies may be ready to launch after Thanksgiving, including Nscale (NSCL), which has a $44.6 billion deal to provide AI computing power to Anthropic. OpenAI, Anthropic's chief rival, is also considering an IPO as soon as 2027.

"However, we will see where Anthropic's trading goes from here and what impact that might have," Smith added.

Retail investors made Thursday the biggest day ever for retail participation in an IPO going back to at least 2012, according to Vanda Research. Demand for shares from Robinhood Markets (HOOD) was "far greater" than it was allocated, its chief executive said.

Meanwhile, institutional investors tend to play the long game and wait for a better price to emerge before buying into a newly public stock, said Baird Managing Director Ted Mortonson. Their decisions in the coming weeks will have a big impact.

Anthropic will also soon start to get added to major stock indices - likely including the Nasdaq-100 NDX. Insider-owned shares subject to early lockups will also begin to expire. Hundreds of millions of shares were released for trading on Thursday, and another 174 million class A shares will be released next month.

"We won't know the depth of demand until we see those shares come unlocked," said Ben Black, chief investment officer at Powerlaw.

-William Gavin

data.title: US Market Crash: Dow Jones tanks 1,100 points, nears technical correction - What is plaguing Wall Street?
data.description:
Benchmark indices on Wall Street ended sharply lower on Thursday, November 19, as the mega and historic listing of Anthropic PBC failed to sustain the enthusiasm around the AI trade as multiple issues continue to bother market participants. The initial bout of gains was quickly sold into and the selling only accelerated through the session.

The Dow Jones tanked 1,100 points on Thursday, taking the four-day fall for the index to 3,250 points. The index had entered a "Technical Correction", meaning a 10% fall from the peak at its intraday low. The index also closed below the mark of 50,000 for the first time since June this year.

The day was no different for the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, as despite the Anthropic listing, other names sold-off and dragged both the indices lower by over 2% each. 460 stocks on the S&P 500 ended with losses on Thursday, indicating the extent of the adverse market breadth.

Wall Street's volatility gauge, the CBOE VIX crossed the mark of 29 intraday and is now at the highest level since March this year.

Anthropic Makes A Historic Debut

Anthropic PBC became the first AI lab to go public, debuting at a hefty premium to its already upsized issue price.

The stock began trading at $111.5 per share, a 34.3% premium to its revised IPO price of $83 apiece. At listing, Anthropic's market capitalization had crossed the mark of $2 trillion.

At the close of the session, Anthropic shares saw some profit booking from the highs to close at $97.7, still a 17% premium from the issue price, valued at $1.8 trillion, making it the seventh most valuable US company.

AMD In The Line Of Fire

After Nvidia, which has now been issued subpoenas by the Attorney General's office in California, its rival Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) fell prey to a short-seller report on Thursday.

The stock fell 8% on Thursday after short-seller Hunterbrook Media, after disclosing short positions on the stock, said that AMD kept supplying new devices to IEIT Systems, a Chinese server manufacturer, despite the company being blacklisted by the US.

Hunterbrook's note also stated that AMD bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong, and also depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.

In response, AMD stated that it remains fully compliant with US export controls and that Hunterbrook has misrepresented its business practices and relationships.

What Are The Issues Plaguing Wall Street?

Anthropic's IPO was supposed to reinstate some faith in the AI trade, but concerns continued to overshadow not just the tech names, but also the entire Wall Street.

Soon after the Anthropic IPO, democrats lashed out at Anthropic, with some calling it a "ticking time bomb" and a "trojan horse" for hackers and foreign adversaries.

The mega capex planned by these companies also remains an area of concern. After massive debt fund raising, SpaceX is now eyeing a debt sale of $32 billion. That, coupled with the credit market stress, fears of higher interest rates for longer, and geopolitical concerns continue to plague Wall Street.

Sell-off also continued in Gold and Silver, with the Yellow Metal now set for its worst losing streak since May, and Silver prices declining over 65% from their peak of over $120 an ounce.
